name: CTF Agent
description: CTF solver that races several models in parallel Docker sandboxes
seenIn: No public report of use in an attack. Covered from its source code

indicators.context: User agent of the CTF Agent CTFd client on every request to the CTFd platform (challenge list and solves polled every 5 seconds, challenge details, file downloads, flag submissions, login). A Windows 7 string cut off before (KHTML, like Gecko): no browser sends it. Match the whole value: as a substring it is the start
indicators.source: ThreatDefence review of the CTF Agent source code

indicators.value: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 6.1; WOW64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/45.0.2454.85 Safari/537.36
indicators.context: User agent of the CTF Agent pull_challenges.py helper on CTFd /login, /challenges and /api/v1/ requests. Taken from es3n1n/Eruditus, which sends the same string, and an old real Chrome string: context only
indicators.source: ThreatDefence review of the CTF Agent source code

indicators.context: First command CTF Agent runs in every new solver sandbox container through the Docker API, inside bash -c, to learn the container architecture (backend/sandbox.py:165-171). Seen where the EDR sensor sees container processes
indicators.source: ThreatDefence review of the CTF Agent source code

indicators.context: Wrapper around every command CTF Agent runs in a solver sandbox: bash -c "timeout --signal=KILL --kill-after=5 <seconds> bash -c '<command>'". Other scripts may use the same timeout options: look for bursts from one container
indicators.source: ThreatDefence review of the CTF Agent source code

indicators.value: IMPORTANT: You are running inside a Docker sandbox. All files are under /challenge/
indicators.context: Start of the system prompt of the CTF Agent Claude and Codex solvers, sent to the model with every request; visible in model traffic with TLS inspection, in Claude Code or Codex session files, and possibly on the claude CLI command line
indicators.source: ThreatDefence review of the CTF Agent source code

indicators.value: You are a CTF competition coordinator running for the ENTIRE duration of a live competition
indicators.context: First line of the CTF Agent coordinator system prompt (Claude and Codex coordinators), sent with every coordinator request
indicators.source: ThreatDefence review of the CTF Agent source code

indicators.value: You are an expert CTF solver. Find the real flag for the challenge below.
indicators.context: First line of the CTF Agent solver prompt built for every challenge; also in the model requests of its Pydantic AI solvers (Bedrock, Azure, Zen, Google)
indicators.source: ThreatDefence review of the CTF Agent source code

indicators.context: Tool name the CTF Agent Claude coordinator sees for its in-process MCP server coordinator (also spawn_swarm, bump_agent, broadcast, kill_swarm); in model requests and Claude Code session transcripts. The server name coordinator is generic: use this tool name, not the prefix
indicators.source: ThreatDefence review of the CTF Agent source code

indicators.context: Docker label key (value true) on every CTF Agent solver container; at start the agent force-deletes every container with this label. Also the project name and Codex clientInfo name, so a bare match is weak: use it as a container label
indicators.source: ThreatDefence review of the CTF Agent source code

indicators.context: Local image CTF Agent runs its solver containers from (docker build -f sandbox/Dockerfile.sandbox -t ctf-sandbox), with SYS_ADMIN, SYS_PTRACE, seccomp unconfined and /dev/loop-control. Not on a registry, generic name: context only
indicators.source: ThreatDefence review of the CTF Agent source code

indicators.context: Prefix of the host temporary folder (tempfile.mkdtemp, /tmp/ctf-workspace-<random> on Linux) each CTF Agent solver sandbox mounts read-write on /challenge/workspace; removed when the solver stops
indicators.source: ThreatDefence review of the CTF Agent source code

indicators.context: CTF Agent per-solver JSONL trace logs/trace-<challenge>-<model>-<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>.jsonl in the working directory (models claude-opus-4-6, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-5.3-codex by default). Generic prefix: confirm with the model name in the file name or the YARA rule
indicators.source: ThreatDefence review of the CTF Agent source code

indicators.context: OpenCode Zen gateway CTF Agent uses for zen/* model specs and as the quota fallback for codex/gpt-5.3-codex-spark. Used by many OpenCode users: context only
